name: Now Hiring!

pick.label: Pick a job
pick.heading: Pick an unusual job and find the perfect person for it
lead: Some jobs are easy to advertise. Others are harder: try writing the job advert for a club bouncer.
Choose a job, and work out what it really involves, who would be perfect for it, and how you would find them. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The stranger the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This isn’t a real HR exercise, it’s just for a bit of fun. All of these jobs really exist: somebody, somewhere, is doing one of them right now.

shelf.head: Only in Berlin
items: Tour guide on a Spree boat

rows: Which job are you hiring for?
The bit nobody puts in the advert: the hours, the smell, the customers…
Skills, personality, experience. What do they need to be good at?
Where would you advertise, or who would you ask?
One task that shows you who can really do the job.
The perk that makes everyone apply:
Free tickets, free ice cream, free… what?

values.really: Saying “Zurückbleiben, bitte!” about four thousand times, and recording 47 different ways of saying that the train is late without sounding guilty.
values.perfect: Someone with a calm voice that sounds kind, but also very slightly disappointed in you. Like your favourite teacher at school.
values.find: On a platform at 8 a.m., listening for the person who sighs most professionally when the train doesn’t come.
values.test: Announce a 20-minute delay on the U8 so warmly that nobody on the platform minds.
values.perk: A free ticket for life, and you get to hear your own voice every morning on the way to work.

yours.label: Your job
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your job and your perfect candidate in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which job would you apply for?
rank.placeholder: The job, e.g. Voice of the U-Bahn
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their job in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees. The winner is the job most of us would apply for.
